notes:
A wasei-eigo (Japanese-coined English) term. In English, these are usually called "paper towels," while "kitchen paper" is more common in British English. In Japan, キッチンペーパー specifically refers to absorbent paper used in cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- キッチンペーパー⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{拭|ふ}く→拭く：04261_fuku⟧: to wipe with kitchen paper
- キッチンペーパー⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{油|あぶら}を{切|き}る→油を切る：22553_aburawokiru⟧: to drain oil with kitchen paper
- キッチンペーパー⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{水気|みずけ}→水気：07952_mizuke⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to pat dry with kitchen paper
- キッチンペーパー⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{包|つつ}む→包む：01226_tsutsumu⟧: to wrap in kitchen paper

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ペーパータオル→ペーパータオル：24995_peepaataoru⟧: paper towel — sometimes used interchangeably, but can also refer to hand-drying towels in restrooms
- ⟦ティッシュ→ティッシュ：08816_tisshu⟧: tissue — thinner and used for wiping the face or nose, not for cooking
- クッキング⟦シート→シート：10945_shiito⟧: cooking sheet, parchment paper — used for baking, not absorbing
